From 5f9b329096596b7e53e07d041d7fca4cbe1be752 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 16:17:44 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] bonding: provide a net pointer to __skb_flow_dissect()

After 3cbf4ffba5ee ("net: plumb network namespace into __skb_flow_dissect")
we have to provide a net pointer to __skb_flow_dissect(),
either via skb->dev, skb->sk, or a user provided pointer.

In the following case, syzbot was able to cook a bare skb.

  do_syscall_x64 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63 [inline]
  do_syscall_64+0xec/0xf80 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94

Fixes: 58deb77cc52d ("bonding: balance ICMP echoes in layer3+4 mode")
Reported-by: syzbot+c46409299c70a221415e@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/696faa23.050a0220.4cb9c.001f.GAE@google.com/T/#u
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Matteo Croce <mcroce@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Stanislav Fomichev <sdf@fomichev.me>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260120161744.1893263-1-edumazet@google.com

diff --git a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
index 0aca6c937297..e7caf400a59c 100644
--- a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
@@ -4096,8 +4096,9 @@ static bool bond_flow_dissect(struct bonding *bond, struct sk_buff *skb, const v
 	case BOND_XMIT_POLICY_ENCAP23:
 	case BOND_XMIT_POLICY_ENCAP34:
 		memset(fk, 0, sizeof(*fk));
-		return __skb_flow_dissect(NULL, skb, &flow_keys_bonding,
-					  fk, data, l2_proto, nhoff, hlen, 0);
+		return __skb_flow_dissect(dev_net(bond->dev), skb,
+					  &flow_keys_bonding, fk, data,
+					  l2_proto, nhoff, hlen, 0);
 	default:
 		break;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c`

- **Change**: In the function `bond_flow_dissect()`, the call to `__skb_flow_dissect()` was modified.
- **Before**: The first argument (`net`) was passed as `NULL`.
- **After**: The first argument is now `dev_net(bond->dev)`, which provides the network namespace of the bonding device.

### Relationship

The modification directly addresses a bug introduced by commit `3cbf4ffba5ee` ("net: plumb network namespace into __skb_flow_dissect"), which made the `net` parameter mandatory to avoid warnings when the skb lacks a valid `skb->dev` or `skb->sk` (e.g., bare skbs from XDP programs). By passing the bonding device’s net namespace, the flow dissector can safely operate without triggering a kernel warning, thus fixing the reported syzbot issue.

Root cause:
The call to __skb_flow_dissect in bond_flow_dissect passed NULL as the net pointer, which is no longer allowed after commit 3cbf4ffba5ee. When a bare skb (without a dev or sk) was processed, the function triggered a WARNING.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
return __skb_flow_dissect(NULL, skb, &flow_keys_bonding, fk, data, l2_proto, nhoff, hlen, 0);
Reason: `__skb_flow_dissect()` requires a non-NULL net pointer after commit 3cbf4ffba5ee. Passing NULL causes a WARNING when the skb lacks a dev or sk, as in a bare skb from XDP.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
return __skb_flow_dissect(dev_net(bond->dev), skb, &flow_keys_bonding, fk, data, l2_proto, nhoff, hlen, 0);
Reason: `dev_net(bond->dev)` provides a valid net pointer from the bonding device, which is always available in this context. This satisfies the requirement of `__skb_flow_dissect()` and prevents the WARNING.

		break;
